{{Short description|American biostatistician}}
'''Debbie Mein-Pay Cheng''' is an American biostatistician and a professor at the [[Boston University School of Public Health]]. She researches applied statistics and [[clinical trial]] design.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Debbie Cheng {{!}} SPH |url=https://www.bu.edu/sph/profile/debbie-cheng/ |access-date=2024-03-02 |website=www.bu.edu}}</ref> Cheng was elected a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 25, 2023 |title=Debbie Cheng Elected Fellow of the American Statistical Association |url=https://www.bu.edu/hic/2023/06/25/hariri-institute-faculty-affiliate-debbie-cheng-sph-named-fellow-of-the-american-statistical-association/ |access-date=2024-03-02 |website=Rafik Hariri Institute for Computing and Computational Science & Engineering}}</ref> She earned a B.S. in industrial engineering from [[Northwestern University]].<ref name=":0" /> She received a Sc.D. in biostatistics from the [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]].<ref name=":0" /> Her 1999 dissertation was titled, ''Analysis of Data from Eradication Studies of Chronic Viral Infections''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis |last=Cheng |first=Debbie M. |title=Analysis of Data from Eradication Studies of Chronic Viral Infections |date=1999 |degree=Sc.D. |publisher=Harvard University |oclc=78782772}}</ref> [[Stephen Lagakos]] was her doctoral advisor.<ref name=":1" />
